intro: Lesson 25: What is soil made of?. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

charts.title: What is in good garden soil?

bullets: Humus from dead plants and animals

panels.title: Where does soil come from?
points: Wind, rain and ice break rock
Hundreds of years for a few centimetres

panels.title: Safety guide: looking at soil
points: An adult says where you may dig
Wear gloves or wash hands well after
Never put soil near your mouth or eyes
Leave worms and minibeasts where you found them

keywords.def: the top layer of the ground that plants grow in
dark material from dead plants and animals that have rotted
comes from something that was once alive
a small amount we collect to look at

questions.q: Name the four things in soil.
questions.a: Rock pieces, humus, air and water

questions.q: Why is topsoil darker than subsoil?
questions.a: It has more humus in it

questions.q: Core: Put a spoonful of soil on white paper. Look closely (use a magnifying glass if you have one). Draw and label what you find.
questions.a: Labels such as small stones, sand grains, bits of leaf or root, a tiny creature, damp patches

questions.q: Extend: Sort your finds into 'was once alive' and 'never alive'.
questions.a: Once alive: leaf bits, roots, twigs. Never alive: stones, sand

questions.q: Stretch: Why might a farmer be worried if heavy rain washes the topsoil away?
questions.a: Topsoil has the humus plants need, and it takes hundreds of years to form again.

options: Dead plants and animals that rotted
questions.a: B) Dead plants and animals that rotted. Humus is organic: it was once alive. Rock pieces are not humus.

questions.q: Big question: what would you find if you dug down deep?
questions.a: Dark topsoil with humus, then lighter subsoil and stones, then rock.
